---
title: "The Social Psychology of Inequality: Perceptions, Emotions, and Justifications In Turbulent Times"
subtitle: "RC42 session · XXI ISA World Congress of Sociology, Gwangju 2027"
date: 2027-07-04
author:
  - "Hye Won Kwon"
categories: [Inequality, Emotions, Meritocracy]
---

This session examines how psychological mechanisms shape individuals' interpretations of inequality across various nations during times of rapid social change. The organizers note a paradox: despite rising income inequality and declining intergenerational mobility — both of which suggest a diminishing role of individual merit — recent studies have documented a paradoxical rise in meritocratic beliefs around the world.

The session welcomes research addressing topics such as how perceptions and emotions reinforce or reduce inequalities; inequality reproduction through daily interactions; psychological justifications for disparities; development of unequal psychological resources; and how emerging technologies like AI influence responses to social disparities.

**Organizer(s)/Chair(s):**

- Hye Won Kwon, Ewha Womans University, South Korea

**Host committee(s):** RC42 Social Psychology
